target_customer: Startups, enterprises and high skill individuals needing US work visas and green cards (O-1, H-1B, L-1, TN, EB-1, EB-2 NIW)
problem: Immigration petitions take attorneys weeks or months and incumbents use legacy tools. LegalOS drafts narratives and evidence with AI and attorneys review and sign.
business_model: AI enabled immigration law practice, per case fees (government fees extra); prices not published

founders.name: Matthew Asir
founders.background_notes: YC page says he grew up in his family's US immigration law firm.

founders.name: Rachel Asir
education: University of Chicago, Economics and Media Studies
founders.background_notes: Co-founded a charity per the YC page.

founders.name: Claire Jutabha
education: USC, BS and MS Computer Science

competitors.name: Alma
competitors.what: Tech enabled full service immigration law firm
competitors.traction_then: 98% approval rate cited in a secondary summary

competitors.name: JustiGuide
competitors.what: AI tool for navigating US immigration, registering as a law firm

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM drafting and evidence compilation on top of standard case workflow. The hard parts are legal quality and attorney review, not research grade technology.

defensibility.rationale: Attorney sign off and a petition corpus help, but several AI immigration firms launched in the same window. Claims such as 100 percent approval are self reported.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorption found; competitors multiplied through 2026.

market_need_then: The company cites more than 1M US work visas a year and slow, manual legacy processes. Founders grew up in a family immigration practice and the company lists startup clients such as Arc Prize on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses legalos.ai; no purchase details found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Speed and reliability claims (48 hours, 40+ years of expertise)

brand_strength.rationale: Early; the name echoes other legal OS products and a Product Hunt listing named LegalOS (Notion for Lawyers) exists, though it is not shown to be the same company.

outcome_analysis: LegalOS is a Winter 2026 company still active with early traction (dozens of filings claimed). Founders have family immigration practice experience, which helps credibility, but competition is crowded and funding facts are unverified.
notes: Funding is unverified and conflicting on aggregators only: about $500K total (pre-seed or seed, Pioneer Fund and Rice Capital named by Caplight, dated between January and April 2026 depending on the aggregator) and a $10M figure on Extruct and Signalbase. None is confirmed by a press release or company source, so no round is recorded. Outcome search found no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs. Competitor snippets lack exact dates for some entries. Undated competitor sources omitted from the list: CaseBlink. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed dated March 2026 is now recorded from VCBacked; another source dates it January 2026 and PitchBook lists a seed in April 2026. The $10M figure on Signalbase and Extruct is unconfirmed and not recorded.
